# Toolroll design language

## System and Library

YouIyouX has two sides, and the tool names say which one you are reading:

| Side | What it holds | Tools | You may |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| System | Approved components, tokens and rules (`youi:` ids), with live usage | `system_*`, `npx -y youiyoux show`, `npx -y youiyoux where`, `npx -y youiyoux check`, `npx -y youiyoux plan` | Build with them |
| Library | Ingested references from outside sources (`lib:` ids) | `library_search`, `library_request`, `npx -y youiyoux library` | Browse and request adoption only |

Elements move `library → candidate → adopted → in-use`. Requesting adoption (library → candidate) is the only move an agent makes; a person approves a candidate into the System, and `in-use` comes from the usage map. Never import, copy or restyle code from a Library item, even when it fits better: draft `library_request {"item": "lib:…", "reason": "…"}` (or `npx -y youiyoux library request <id> --reason …`), put the draft in your summary, and build with the System element it would swap in for.

## Build a screen

1. Find what exists: Before creating a UI component, call `ui_find_component` (MCP server `youiyoux`) with the need in words ("dismissible alert", "primary button with icon"): reuse the existing component it names, with its import and props; only when it says nothing fits, start where it says. `system_search` and the component list below cover the System. Prefer an existing component over new markup.
2. Read the contract before using props: `system_get_component {"name": "Button"}`, or `npx -y youiyoux show button` without MCP. Use only the listed values; `guidance` says when to use which.
3. Import from `src/browser/kit` (by a relative path from your file). Never import a component of the same name from anywhere else.
4. Colour, type, radius and shadow come from tokens: `system_get_tokens {"group": "color"}` gives each token's CSS variable and a Tailwind utility (a colour works with bg-, text- and border-). Never write a hex, rgb() or a `[arbitrary]` value that copies a token.
5. See it: after changing a component, call `ui_render {"target": "<file>"}` (or `npx -y youiyoux render <file>`) and open the images it names: light and dark at desktop and phone width, accessibility issues, and a diff against the base commit. Fix its issues, then render again.
6. Run `npx -y youiyoux check` and fix every error; warnings need a reason if left.
- Run from the repo root. After UI edits, run `npx -y youiyoux check --diff` (`--json` for data): it lists what your change adds that near-duplicates an existing component, hardcodes a value a token holds, or imports an element from a library other than the project's choice, each with its fix. Apply each fix.

## Fix a violation

Each finding names its rule, the file:line and a suggestion. The suggested token is an exact value match: confirm the role before using it.

| Rule | Severity | Do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color.no-raw-color` | error | Never hard-code a colour: use token utilities (bg-paper, text-muted-foreground, border-border) or var(--so-*), and look up the role with system_get_tokens. |
| `components.canonical-import` | error | Import kit components only from src/browser/kit (index.js); never define or import another KButton, KChip or KComposer. Server pages use the same markup from src/server/kit.ts. |
| `components.no-native-controls` | warn | Use <KButton>, <KInput>, <KTextarea> and <KComposer> from src/browser/kit; never style a native <button> yourself. |
| `props.contract-values` | error | Call system_get_component before using a component's props; use only the listed values. |
| `tokens.no-arbitrary-values` | warn | Prefer token utilities (rounded-card, text-label, shadow-pill) over [arbitrary] values; youi check suggests the utility. |

## Find where something is used

`npx -y youiyoux where button` lists sites by screen, with prop usage and anything the scanner could not resolve (unknown is never counted as zero). Filter with `--route /settings`. MCP: `system_where_used`, and `system_screen_bom {"route": "/settings"}` for everything on one screen.

## Propose a change to the System

1. Plan it: `npx -y youiyoux plan button --patch '{"status": "deprecated"}'` (or `system_plan`). The plan computes the change class, semver bump, affected screens and which call sites a codemod can rewrite.
2. Put the plan in your summary or PR description for a person to approve. Agents never approve, publish or merge design changes.
3. Never hand-edit `@generated by youi` files; they are rewritten on the next sync.

## Components

- **KActs**: An action bar: one row of actions, 8px apart.
- **KApprove**: The approve control: a password popover only when the rules say so, one click otherwise, nothing when a rule approves automatically. (kind: none|standard|step-up|way-in)
- **KButton**: Every act a person can take. Ink primary for the screen's one act; outline and ghost for the rest; danger for an irreversible act. (variant: primary|outline|ghost|danger; iconOnly: plus|send|stop|x|back|menu|search|chevron|check|alert|more|file|minus|fit|bolt|code; lead: plus|send|stop|x|back|menu|search|chevron|check|alert|more|file|minus|fit|bolt|code)
- **KChip**: Status chips: the five words (Needs you, Running, Queued, Finished, Failed), one tone each; a specific ask keeps its group's tone. (tone: |needs|ask|live|done|failed)
- **KComposer**: The message box: one soft rounded box, auto-growing textarea (rows → 8 lines), + menu, the project as a quiet chip, small controls, and the round send that becomes Stop while the work runs.
- **KCount**: A count pill in tabular figures; ink only for a Needs-you count, muted at zero.
- **KDisclose**: A disclosure for secondary detail (diagnostics, provenance, exact scope).
- **KDocHeader**: A reading page: the 760px column (KDoc), a back link, the one h1 and a meta line (KDocHeader).
- **KDock**: The phone dock: the screen's one primary (the same act its card hides on a phone).
- **KEmpty**: The one empty state: a sentence and one action.
- **KFacts**: Facts: a key/value list (task details, a run's record, an audit entry).
- **KField**: A field: label, the control, one hint line, and the error tied to the control (aria-invalid, aria-describedby). Errors appear next to the control, never as a banner.
- **KFormRow**: The two-column settings row: label and one muted line | the control; stacks on a phone. (variant: |inline|top|wide)
- **KIcon**: One 24×24 stroke icon from the kit set, drawn in currentColor. (name: plus|send|stop|x|back|menu|search|chevron|check|alert|more|file|minus|fit|bolt|code)
- **KNeedsPanel**: Waits that aren't tasks (a spend limit, a failed backup), on their own page: one amber outline, a count, one action each. Never part of the global Needs-you count.
- **KNotFound**: The not-found page inside the shell: what was asked for and two ways on.
- **KNotice**: A refusal in place (role=alert: what went wrong and what didn't change), a neutral system line, or a muted supporting note. There are no toasts.
- **KOverlay**: Popover, drawer, sheet and menu: role=dialog, the app behind inert, Tab kept inside, Escape / Close / scrim close it, focus returns to the trigger. Bordered, never a shadow. (kind: popover|drawer|sheet|menu)
- **KPageHeader**: A list page's header: the phone header (back · title · one trailing action) and the 48px desk top bar (title · muted context · tools).
- **KRadios**: Radio cards: one choice from a few, each with a bold label and one muted line.
- **KRow**: A list row between hairlines under a group heading: chip · title (the whole row is the link) · one muted line · meta · one action in one column.
- **KSeg**: The segmented track: filters or views of one list (aria-pressed).
- **KSelect**: A native select with the kit chevron: 32px, sm 28px in a toolbar, 44px and 16px on a phone.
- **KSettingsShell**: The Settings frame: Overview and the eight groups, a desk breadcrumb, a phone back header, one 760px column.
- **KSlots**: The approval box: status (chip + heading) · supporting text · actions · terms, and the error slot. The same slots in every state, so nothing moves.
- **KSwitch**: An on/off setting: KSwitch acts at once and says its state in words; KSwitchInput is a checkbox with role=switch for a form.
- **KTabs**: Underline tabs for sections of one object: KLinkTabs when each is an address (aria-current="page"), KTabs inside one page (role=tablist, arrow keys).
- **KTiming**: A run's steps on one elapsed-time axis (Release, a flow's run, a pull request's checks); a queued row has no bar until it starts.
